definition: The process of guiding new users through initial setup, training, and adoption of a software platform.
extendedDefinition: Onboarding is the process of guiding new users from first login to regular, productive use of a software product, and it is the strongest predictor of whether an investment produces value. Weak onboarding is a leading cause of abandoned tools, where licenses renew but usage stagnates. Effective onboarding combines structured setup, role-based training, templates, and early wins that show value within the first weeks. Buyers should evaluate onboarding during trials by looking at guided tours, documentation quality, sample data, and support responsiveness for new users. Larger deployments benefit from onboarding plans covering administrator training, data migration, and integration configuration before the user base expands. Metrics worth tracking after rollout include activation rates, feature adoption, and time-to-first-value, since these reveal whether training is sufficient. Vendors that invest in onboarding lower the buyer's implementation cost and improve long-term retention for both sides.
